chunks: 1 - Allah has mercy on him, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who said: 'Ali ibn Mansur narrated to me, saying: I heard Hisham ibn al-Hakam say: Abu Shakir al-Daysani entered the presence of Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him).

He said to him: 'Verily, you are one of the shining stars, and your forefathers were brilliant full-moons, and your foremothers were the wisest of women. Your origin is the most honorable of origins. When the learned are mentioned, you are at the top of the list. Inform me, O Ocean (of Knowledge) that surges with abundance, what is the proof for the emergence of the universe?'

Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) answered: 'We prove it by the things closest to us.' He asked: 'What is that?' He said: So Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) asked for an egg and placed it on his palm, and said: 'This is a fortified container, its interior is smooth, thin, and delicate, containing flowing silver and flowing gold. Then it splits open to reveal something like a peacock. Has anything entered it?' He replied: 'No.'

The Imam said: 'Then this is the proof for the emergence of the universe.' He responded: 'You informed me and were concise, and you spoke and did well. We know that we do not accept anything unless we perceive it with our eyes, or hear it with our ears, or smell it with our nostrils, or taste it with our mouths, or touch it with our hands, or it is clearly imagined in our hearts, or deduced by the narrators with certainty.'
Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have mentioned the five senses, but they are not useful without proof, just as darkness is not dispelled without a lamp.'

key_terms.حَدَثِ الْعَالَمِ: Emergence of the universe (creation having a beginning)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq use the example of an egg to prove the emergence of the universe?
ai.summary: In this dialogue with the Christian philosopher Abu Shakir al-Daysani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the empirical observation of an egg to illustrate the principle of *huduth* (emergence) through internal potentiality rather than external imposition. This narrative underscores the Shia epistemological stance that while sensory perception (*hiss*) provides the data, rational deduction (*aql*) is the necessary lamp to interpret reality, bridging the gap between the visible and the metaphysical. The exchange highlights the compatibility of rational theology with sensory experience, a hallmark of the Kalam tradition in Shia scholarship.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy o him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id that `Ali ibn Mansur related to me that I heard Hisham ibn al-Hakam that Abu Shakir al-Daysani entered the presence of Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

and said to him, Verily, you are one of the shining stars, while your forefathers (AS) were brilliant full-moons, and your foremothers were the wisest of women. Your origin is the most honorable origins. When the learned are mentioned then you are at the top of the list. Inform me, O Ocean (of Knowledge)! How can one prove the emergence of the universe?”

Abu `Abd Allah (AS) answered, “Through reason and by comparing it to the things which are closest to us.” He asked, “What would that be?” The reporter says: Abu `Abd Allah (AS) asked for an egg and placed it on his palm and said: “This is a container. Inside its shell are the albumin, and the egg-yolk. With time, colorful peacock feathers will burst out of it. Has anything entered it?” He replied, “No.”

The Imam (AS) said: “Then this is a proof of the emergence of the universe.” He responded, “Your answer is both nice an concise. I now understand that we cannot accept anything unless we see it with our eyes, here it with our ears, smell it with our noses, taste it with our tongues, touch it with our hands, or feel it in our hearts with certainty.”
Abu `Abd Allah (AS) said: “You have mentioned the five senses. However, they are not useful without proof, in the same way that darkness cannot be prevented but by light.”
